title: Claude Opus 4.8 Outperforms Human Experts on All Measures of Peer Review
summary:
A study of 1,124 academic papers found that reviews produced by Claude Opus 4.8 had a 5.5% error rate, while reviews written by well-paid human experts had a 15.9% error rate. The Harvard research used blind testing where former journal editors preferred the AI's reviews 87% of the time, while GPT-5.5 selected the AI review in all 132 decided pairs of reviews.

The researchers used 134 human reviews from rapidPeer, a Harvard service for expert reviewers, to compare against the AI. The findings reverse previous conclusions that AI should only assist human peer reviewers, suggesting the technology can now handle the first full review pass of expert critiques.

selectedTweets.text:
Massive. New Harvard study finds that AI-written paper reviews now beat the best human peer reviews on every measure the authors tested.

Peer review is slow and often misses errors. Earlier studies concluded AI should only assist human reviewers, not replace them.

They used 134 reviews from rapidPeer, a Harvard service that pays expert reviewers well. Claude Opus 4.8 reviewed the same 1124 papers, and GPT-5.5 plus 3 former journal editors judged the pairs blind.

GPT-5.5 picked the AI review in all 132 decided pairs, and the editors picked it 87% of the time. Only 5.5% of the AI's claims about the paper were wrong, versus 15.9% for the human reviews.

Teams that depend on expert critique can now let AI do the first full review pass, and keep a human for the final decision.
